candidates.description: The isRedirectAllowed function uses url.includes(allowedUrl) instead of url.startsWith(allowedUrl), allowing an attacker to embed an allowed URL as a substring within a malicious URL to bypass the allowlist check.
candidates.rationale: Line 136 uses includes() for allowlist matching. routes/redirect.ts line 15 gates res.redirect(toUrl) on this check. A URL like https://evil.com/?x=https://github.com/juice-shop/juice-shop passes includes() but redirects to evil.com. Verification: request /redirect?to=https://evil.com/?x=https://github.com/juice-shop/juice-shop and observe 302 to evil.com.
candidates.title: Open redirect via substring matching in isRedirectAllowed

candidates.description: The b2bOrder handler passes user-supplied orderLinesData into vm.runInContext with safeEval. While notevil restricts some operations, the vm module is known to be escapable.
candidates.rationale: Line 19 reads body.orderLinesData from the request. Line 23 evaluates it via vm.runInContext('safeEval(orderLinesData)', sandbox). The route is mounted at /b2b/v2 with isAuthorized() middleware. Verification: POST to /b2b/v2 with a payload that triggers a vm escape primitive and observe whether it executes outside the sandbox.
candidates.title: User-controlled input evaluated in vm.runInContext via safeEval

candidates.description: handleYamlUpload passes user-controlled file content to yaml.load within a vm.runInContext call. YAML deserialization can trigger prototype pollution or resource exhaustion even inside a VM sandbox.
candidates.rationale: Line 105 reads file.buffer.toString() from the uploaded file. Line 109 calls vm.runInContext('JSON.stringify(yaml.load(data))', sandbox). The route is POST /file-upload. Verification: upload a .yml file with a crafted YAML payload (e.g., deep nesting or alias bomb) and observe whether it causes DoS or escapes the sandbox.
candidates.title: User-uploaded YAML parsed with yaml.load inside vm.runInContext
